title: Artificial Intelligence
subject: ai-ds
description: A foundational course on the design of intelligent agents, covering the history of AI, search and game playing, logical knowledge representation and probabilistic reasoning under uncertainty.

units.title: Unit 1 · Foundations & Intelligent Agents
units.description: What AI is, how the field developed, and the rational-agent framework used throughout the course.

topics.title: What is AI? History and Approaches
topics.description: The four approaches to defining AI, the Turing test, rationality, and a timeline of the field from 1943 to the deep learning era.

documents.title: What is AI? History and Approaches — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Definitions of AI along the human/rational and thinking/acting axes, the Turing test, and key milestones including Dartmouth 1956 and the AI winters.

topics.title: Intelligent Agents and Environments
topics.description: Agents, agent functions, PEAS task descriptions, properties of task environments and the five agent architectures.

documents.title: Intelligent Agents and Environments — Lecture Notes
documents.description: PEAS descriptions, the seven environment dimensions with classified examples, and reflex, model-based, goal-based, utility-based and learning agents.

units.title: Unit 2 · Search & Problem Solving
units.description: Formulating problems as state-space search, blind and heuristic search strategies, and search in two-player games.

topics.title: Uninformed Search
topics.description: Problem formulation and the blind search strategies BFS, uniform-cost, DFS, depth-limited and iterative deepening search.

documents.title: Uninformed Search Strategies — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Completeness, optimality, time and space complexity of uninformed search strategies in b, d, m notation.

topics.title: Informed Search and Heuristics
topics.description: Heuristic search with greedy best-first and A*, properties of heuristics, and adversarial search in games.

documents.title: Informed Search and Heuristics — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Greedy best-first search, A*, admissible and consistent heuristics, A* optimality proof and 8-puzzle heuristics.

documents.title: Adversarial Search: Minimax and Alpha-Beta Pruning
documents.description: Game formulation, a fully worked minimax and alpha-beta example, move ordering and the O(b^(m/2)) best case.

units.title: Unit 3 · Knowledge, Reasoning & Uncertainty
units.description: Representing knowledge in propositional and first-order logic, logical inference, and reasoning with probabilities and Bayesian networks.

topics.title: Propositional and First-Order Logic
topics.description: Syntax and semantics of propositional and first-order logic, entailment, inference rules, resolution and chaining.

documents.title: Propositional and First-Order Logic — Lecture Notes
documents.description: Syntax, semantics, entailment, validity and satisfiability, inference rules and quantifiers in first-order logic.

documents.title: Resolution, CNF and Chaining — Worked Examples
documents.description: Step-by-step CNF conversion, resolution refutation proofs, and forward and backward chaining on Horn clauses.

topics.title: Probabilistic Reasoning and Bayesian Networks
topics.description: Bayes' rule, conditional independence, Bayesian networks, exact inference by enumeration and the Naive Bayes model.

documents.title: Probabilistic Reasoning and Bayesian Networks — Lecture Notes
documents.description: A medical-test Bayes' rule example, the burglary alarm network, inference by enumeration and Naive Bayes classification.
